task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name is assembled from adjusted character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The target state code is carried through runtime-derived transport keys and recovered shortly before console output.
The submit route selects its live configuration only after click-time DOM, form-order, style and dataset state are captured.

The click path crosses delegated event handling, action routing, gate checks, tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling, local event dispatch, runtime slot materialization, state encoding, dynamic transport and sink wrapping.
The same submit interaction emits non-target prepare/audit objects carrying state_code-like values before the target account.submit object.
The deployed bundle also contains proof-like and vendor-like decoys that execute or remain reachable-looking without feeding the target state_code field.

Construct validity note: several score>=0.5 answer_function names remain readable in the bundle (renameGlobals:false); the practical bottleneck is semantic disambiguation within that candidate set, not merely finding the encoding chain.
The target value is separated from the click by Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame, MutationObserver and DOM CustomEvent boundaries.
The selected runtime configuration is cloned and mutated in a WeakMap-backed materialization step before the encoder receives it.
The final sink receives an already encoded value after dynamic cell and lane recovery, so sink inspection alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.subtype: click-time form and configuration state code
behavior_category.reason: The observable value is a stable compact encoding of form fields, route/config state and click-time runtime state. It is not a request signature, browser fingerprint, byte-array transform or request-body rewrite.

near_categories.why_not: The output has no proof/token/seal semantics; proof-like code in the bundle is decoy material and does not feed the target field.
No network request body is emitted or rewritten; the target is a console-observable state code.
The chain uses local DOM state, not browser/device capability collection as the target behavior.
